mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the next 60 days indicates a shift to accommodative monetary policy, which lowers discount rates and increases the present value of future equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of 60-day easing windows despite the signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing discount rates and reducing the present value of future cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of tightening windows despite the signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) over the next 60 days signals a strengthening labor market, which reduces the cost of capital and increases the present value of equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of strengthening windows despite the signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
